disposition_reason: Table 3 prints mean ± SD Cr, Cd, Pb, Cu, Ni, Mn, Zn, Fe and Sn (mg/kg) in three brands each of cheese, yoghurt and butter bought in Enugu State, Nigeria; lead was not detected in any product.

study.design: Retail market survey of dairy products with health risk index
study.origin: brand countries of origin: Nigeria, Malaysia, France, Austria, South Africa
study.market: local markets in Nsukka and Enugu, Enugu State, Nigeria
study.method: HNO3:HClO4 (4:1) digestion of 2 g at 70 °C; flame AAS (AA-7000)
lod: LOD 0.00001 ppm for Cr, Cd, Pb, Cu, Ni, Mn, Zn, Fe; LOQ 0.0001-0.0002 ppm (Table 2); Sn not listed
study.qa: Spike recoveries 87.5% (Pb) to 105.27% (Ni); triplicate analyses; no CRM

unresolved: Cheese variety is not stated for any brand; recorded as generic cheese only.
A flame AAS LOD of 0.00001 ppm (0.01 µg/kg) is implausibly low for this technique.
Table 2 unspiked nickel (0.8947 ppm) differs from the Table 3 PLTC nickel (0.8547 mg/kg).
The text attaches the BB butter means to the wrong metals in its intake paragraph (e.g. 0.0431 called Pb), contradicting Table 3 where Pb is ND.
Health risk index values (Table 4) are derived and not recorded.
